bills.title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
bills.status: Message on Senate action sent to the House.
bills.nexus: H.R. 6500 directly implicates the Office of Management and Budget and Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service, as a continuing resolution governs the apportionment of funds and Treasury's cash management and debt issuance authorities for the duration of the stopgap period. The implementation risk centers on Treasury's ability to execute borrowing operations and agency payment processing without a lapse that could trigger cash flow constraints or disrupt Fiscal Service systems supporting government-wide appropriations accounting.

bills.title: Promoting National Service and Reducing Unemployment Act
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on Appropriations, and in addition to the Committee on Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: Without a known nexus to Treasury authorities or offices, this bill appears to fall primarily within the jurisdiction of the Committees on Appropriations and Education and Workforce, touching national service programming and labor market policy rather than tax, finance, or financial regulation functions. Treasury Legislative Affairs should monitor for any tax credit, bond financing, or payroll-related provisions that could engage IRS, OTA, or Fiscal Service equities during markup.

bills.title: Emergency Savings Enhancement Act of 2025
bills.status: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 544.
bills.nexus: S. 3333 would likely amend the Internal Revenue Code to expand or create tax-advantaged emergency savings mechanisms, directly implicating IRS rulemaking authority under the Office of Tax Policy and the IRS. Treasury's implementation risk centers on designing qualifying account rules, employer plan integration guidance, and potential revenue cost estimates that must be scored before floor consideration.

bills.title: First-Time Home Buyer Empowerment Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5227 falls squarely within Treasury's purview because any new first-time homebuyer tax credit or savings incentive would be administered by IRS and would require Office of Tax Policy to draft guidance and revenue estimates. The implementation risk centers on accurately scoring the cost of the credit, preventing improper claims at scale, and coordinating with HUD on eligibility definitions to avoid compliance gaps.

bills.title: Senior Accessible Housing Tax Credit Act of 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: Treasury cares because S. 5216 would create a new tax credit administered through the Internal Revenue Code, directly implicating IRS's authority to design guidance, eligibility rules, and compliance mechanisms. The implementation risk centers on IRS and the Office of Tax Policy needing to define "accessible housing" standards, coordinate with HUD on qualifying criteria, and manage potential interactions with existing Low-Income Housing Tax Credit rules under Section 42.

bills.title: Making appropriations for national security, Department of State, and related programs for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, and for other purposes.
bills.nexus: H.R. 8595 directly funds programs administered through Treasury's Office of Terrorism and Financial Intelligence (TFI) and touches sanctions-related authorities under IEEPA and OFAC that depend on annual appropriations for staffing and operations. If the bill stalls or is amended in the Senate, Treasury faces the risk of a funding gap that could impair sanctions enforcement, financial intelligence activities, and interagency coordination on national security financial policy.

bills.title: Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027
bills.nexus: H.R. 9770 directly funds Treasury's annual operating appropriations, covering offices such as IRS, the Departmental Offices, and the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network through the continuing resolution period. Without enacted appropriations, Treasury faces operating constraints, potential lapses in tax administration and financial intelligence functions, and disruption to debt management operations under the authority of the Fiscal Assistant Secretary.

bills.title: Senior Accessible Housing Tax Credit Act of 2026
bills.status: Sponsor introductory remarks on measure. (CR H4413)
bills.nexus: H.R. 9554 proposes a new tax credit targeting senior housing construction and rehabilitation, directly engaging the Internal Revenue Service (under Treasury's supervision) and the Office of Tax Policy to design and administer eligibility rules, credit calculations, and compliance mechanisms. Treasury faces implementation risk in standing up a novel credit structure, including guidance issuance, potential interaction with existing Low-Income Housing Tax Credit provisions, and revenue cost estimation for scoring purposes.

bills.title: First-Time Home Buyer Empowerment Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7468 falls under Treasury's purview because it would amend the Internal Revenue Code to create or expand a tax benefit for first-time homebuyers, directly engaging the IRS's administration of individual income tax provisions and the Office of Tax Policy's revenue-scoring responsibilities. The implementation risk centers on IRS's capacity to verify eligibility, design compliant forms and guidance, and absorb the revenue cost estimated by Joint Committee on Taxation.
